newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus says protesters plotting coup.
newsitem.headline: Belarus says protesters plotting coup.

text.p: Belarus authorities said on Friday they had launched an investigation into a coup plot after arresting a man who passed out fliers on the street.

Minsk public prosecutor Nikolai Kupriyanov said extremists planned to use an anti-government rally on the 11th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster on Saturday to foment violence against the government.
"A government coup is the most serious crime according to Belarus law," he said on local radio. "Even the death penalty could be used in such cases."

He said police had arrested one man who passed out fliers urging people to bring sticks, stones, bottles and other potential weapons to the Saturday demonstration, which organisers hope will attract 20-30,000 people.
Others were also involved in calling for violence in pamphlets distributed across the city, he said. No such pamphlets were spotted, however, during a walk in central Minsk.
Authoritarian President Alexander Lukashenko, who is in Vietnam on an eight-day tour of Asia, said before his departure that any extremist acts in his absence would be considered a government coup.

The Chernobyl anniversary has became a catalyst for anti-Lukashenko demonstrations, and inspired a protest last year. But in recent months Lukashenko has taken an increasingly hard line against dissent in the ex-Soviet republic located between Russia and Poland.

The head of Minsk police, Boris Tarletsky, saying he was concerned about possible violence on Saturday, also made a radio appeal for calm. "I call for police tomorrow to keep order and not submit to provocations," he said.
Belarus, located downwind from Chernobyl, is one of several nations expected to mark the anniversary of the April 26, 1986 Chernobyl disaster.
